question: The transition to more sustainable agricultural practices that contribute to climate mitigation, adaptation and the restoration of ecosystems is a challenging process. In this context, regenerative agriculture, with its focus on soil health, carbon sequestration, water retention and biodiversity enhancement, is increasingly recognised as a promising approach to address these interconnected challenges.

Despite its potential benefits, regenerative agriculture is not yet defined within EU policies. Farmers willing to adopt such practices often face barriers, including limited financial incentives, technical support and market recognition. 1.
How does the Commission intend to support and integrate regenerative agriculture in order to ensure consistency between policy design, funding and monitoring at EU level?

What measures will the Commission take to promote research, innovation and knowledge transfer on regenerative farming systems and to ensure that small and medium-sized farms can benefit from these advances?
Does the Commission plan to strengthen financial and technical support for farmers who adopt regenerative agricultural practices?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2025) 1. The Vision for agriculture and food highlights the need to ensure soil health and sustainable management of natural resources1. Regenerative agriculture can help address these challenges in synergy with the Water Resilience Strategy2, the Soil Monitoring Law3, and the EU climate adaptation plan4.

Under the current Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), 32% of the funds are dedicated to environmental and climate objectives, including soil health, water management and biodiversity protection5. Member States design specific support schemes in their CAP Strategic Plans and have included support for many regenerative practices. 2.

Under Horizon Europe (2021-2027)6, the Commission is funding several Research and Innovation projects7 and initiatives relating to Regenerative agriculture (including support dedicated to regenerative farming practices), such as CoFund Partnership on Agroecology8, and the EU Mission ‘A Soil Deal for Europe’9.

The European Innovation Partnership for Agricultural Productivity and Sustainability (EIP-AGRI) promotes over 70 Operational Group projects10 testing innovative regenerative agriculture practices. The EU CAP Network, through its dedicated Focus Group on Regenerative Agriculture11, collects and disseminates the resulting knowledge.

The CAP also supports Member States in strengthening their farm advisory services, thus ensuring these innovations reach the farm level. 3. The proposals for the CAP after 202712, provide tools to support regenerative and other forms of sustainable agriculture.

Moreover, as stated in the Vision for Agriculture and Food, the Commission will develop a voluntary on-farm sustainability compass, including possible indicators in line with regenerative agriculture.

1 A vision for Agriculture and Food, COM(2025) final. 2 European Water Resilience Strategy, A vision for Agriculture and Food, COM(2025) 280 final. 3 Proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on Soil Monitoring and Resilience (Soil
Monitoring Law), COM(2023) 416 Final. 4 to be published in 2026.

5 The green architecture of the current Agricultural Policy (2023-2027) provides a set of Good Agricultural and Environmental Conditions (GAEC) and Statutory Management Requirements as compulsory requirements, as well as voluntary schemes, such as eco-schemes, and rural development intervention for environmental, climate and animal welfare (agri-environment-climate commitments, areas with natural or other area-specific constraints, Natura 2000 and Water Framework Directive payments, and green investments).

10 The list of projects can be found on the following link: https://eu-cap-network.ec.europa.eu/projects/search_en. 11 The final report, factsheet and other elements regarding the focus group can be found on the following link: https://eu-cap-network.ec.europa.eu/focus-group-regenerative-agriculture-soil-health_en. 12 https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/media/news/next-chapter-cap-2025-07-17_en.
